Audit verdict: ACCEPTThe mathematical reduction is sound within its stated scope. In particular, the four-copy construction correctly closes every owner component, including isolated vertices, without sacrificing the original physical edges or the matching-transfer argument.The important distinction is:Proved: the unrestricted physical problem reduces exactly to the class with  $Q$  perfect and  $B$  2-regular.Not proved: the target inequality on that remaining class.Also proved conditionally: the two-copy short-class refinement retains its quantitative path-surplus bound.Not claimed: preservation of that refinement by the four-copy construction.I distinguish the original two-copy proposal's independent Oracle provenance from the subsequent four-copy deduction. Neither is a claim of literature priority.1. Mathematical argument audit1.1 Original physical domainLet  $V$  have  $N=2b$  indices. The physical graph has three vertex layers: $b$  helpers, each joined to the two endpoints of one  $P$ -edge; $N$  witnesses, joined according to  $Q$ ; $N$  owners, with owner graph  $B$ , and one witness-owner edge per index.The physical colouring is constant on  $P$  and changes across  $Q$  and  $B$ .Since  $P$  is a perfect matching and  $Q$  is a partial matching,  $A=P\cup Q$  has maximum degree two. Its components are alternating paths and cycles. The physical colouring forces every auxiliary cycle to have length divisible by four. Likewise,  $B$  has path and even-cycle components.The permission condition is
$$U\text{ permitted}
\iff
\Delta(B[V\setminus U])\leq1.$$
The matching identity is
$$\beta_I
=b+|V\setminus U|+\alpha(A[U])
=3b-\nu(A[U])$$
after maximizing the independent witness set for a fixed permitted  $U$ . Consequently,
$$\tau(A,B)\leq\lfloor N/6\rfloor$$
is exactly the all-helper  $8b/3$  target.There is no need for the invalid mixed identity  $\beta_I=2b+h$ .1.2 Two-copy auxiliary completionCorrectThe endpoint parity calculation is decisive.For an auxiliary path of order  $m$ , its edges alternate beginning and ending with  $P$ . The number of  $Q$ -edges is
$$\frac m2-1.$$
Therefore:PathNumber of Q edgesEndpoint coloursCompletion $P_{4k}$  $2k-1$ OppositeClose each copy internally $P_{4k+2}$  $2k$ EqualJoin corresponding endpoints across copiesFor  $P_{4k}$ , the new endpoint edge is a valid  $Q$ -edge in each copy. The smallest case is  $P_4$ , so its endpoints were not already adjacent.For  $P_{4k+2}$ , the second copy reverses physical colouring. The cross-copy endpoint edges therefore join opposite colours. The smallest case  $P_2$  gives a simple four-cycle:
$$a_0-b_0-b_1-a_1-a_0.$$
There is no repeated edge.Original auxiliary cycles remain unchanged. Every unmatched endpoint receives exactly one new  $Q$ -edge. Thus: $P$  remains perfect; $Q$  becomes perfect;every component of  $A$  becomes a  $C_{4k}$ ;every original physical edge is retained.The construction is valid without assuming any certificate for the remaining cyclic inequality.1.3 Four-copy owner completionCorrect, including isolatesThe four-copy construction uses the two pairs  $(0,1)$  and  $(2,3)$  for auxiliary completion, with
$$c(v_j)=c(v)\oplus(j\bmod 2).$$
The owner construction has three cases.Even owner cycles. Keep all four copies. They remain even cycles.Owner paths of order  $l\geq2$ . For endpoints  $x,y$ , add
$$x_0x_1,\quad y_0y_1,\quad
x_2x_3,\quad y_2y_3.$$
Each pair of copies forms one cycle of order  $2l$ .This includes the important  $l=2$  case: an original owner edge is retained and the added edges complete a simple  $C_4$ .Owner isolates. For an isolate  $v$ , add
$$v_0v_1,\quad v_1v_2,\quad
v_2v_3,\quad v_3v_0.$$
This produces a simple  $C_4$ . All four vertices receive their two required owner neighbours.Every added owner edge joins copies with opposite physical colours. Distinct original owner components have disjoint supports, so their closure edges cannot conflict.The resulting owner graph is precisely 2-regular.The degree audit is:Physical vertex typeCompleted degreeHelper2Witness3Owner3The index graphs  $A$  and  $B$  are both 2-regular, and the physical graph remains bipartite and subcubic.One important qualification is correctly recorded in the manuscript: the four owner copies are no longer disjoint copies of the original owner graph. That does not invalidate transfer. All original owner edges remain, and permission is hereditary under edge and vertex deletion.In particular, arbitrary crossings between auxiliary and owner components do not obstruct this construction. Auxiliary completion and owner completion operate on different physical edge layers.1.4 Exact matching transferCorrectThis is the central argument, and it does not require any allocation of matching credit to individual components.Let  $\widehat U$  be a permitted omission in a  $t$ -copy completion. Define
$$U_j=\{v:v_j\in\widehat U\}.$$
Because every original owner edge in each copy is retained,
$$\Delta(B[V\setminus U_j])\leq1.$$
Thus every  $U_j$  is an original permitted omission.Choose an original maximum matching
$$M_j\subseteq A[U_j].$$
All its edges occur in the corresponding copy of the completed auxiliary graph. Since different copies have disjoint vertex sets,
$$\bigcup_{j=1}^{t}M_j$$
is a genuine matching in  $\widehat A[\widehat U]$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{
\sum_{j=1}^{t}\nu(A[U_j])
\leq \nu(\widehat A[\widehat U]).
}
\tag{2}$$
This is an inequality, not an equality. Added auxiliary edges may increase the completed matching number.If the completed certificate meets its target,
$$\nu(\widehat A[\widehat U])
\leq\left\lfloor\frac{tN}{6}\right\rfloor,$$
then the cheapest original copy satisfies
$$\begin{aligned}
\min_j\nu(A[U_j])
&\leq
\left\lfloor
\frac{\sum_j\nu(A[U_j])}{t}
\right\rfloor\\
&\leq
\left\lfloor
\frac{\lfloor tN/6\rfloor}{t}
\right\rfloor\\
&=\left\lfloor\frac N6\right\rfloor.
\end{aligned}$$
The last identity is valid for every integer  $N$  and positive integer  $t$ . Writing  $N/6=q+r$ , with  $0\leq r<1$ , proves it immediately.No divisibility assumption is missing.The final original physical certificate is reconstructed using the original graph: select all helpers, the original owners  $V\setminus U_j$ , and a maximum independent set of the original  $A[U_j]$ . Its size is
$$3b-\nu(A[U_j]).$$
The added edges are never used as physical edges in this certificate.1.5 Exact equivalence of the restricted problemsThe two-copy result proves
$$\boxed{
\text{Universal physical target}
\iff
\text{target for }Q\text{-perfect templates}.
}$$
Since  $P$  and  $Q$  are then perfect, their alternating union consists of  $C_{4k}$  components.The four-copy result strengthens the restriction:
$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Universal physical target}\\
&\iff
\text{target for }Q\text{-perfect templates with }B
\text{ a union of even cycles}.
\end{aligned}
}$$
The reverse directions are immediate restrictions of the universal statement. The forward directions follow from the explicit completions and transfer.This is a genuine equivalence of universal assertions, not merely an implication for a special family.It does not establish the target on the restricted family.2. Counterexample localizationThe connected-component argument is also correct.In the completed class, permission separates across connected components of  $A\cup B$ , and matching number is additive. Therefore
$$\tau(A,B)=\sum_i\tau_i.$$
Every component consists of whole auxiliary cycles, so its order  $N_i$  is divisible by four.If every component satisfies
$$\tau_i\leq\lfloor N_i/6\rfloor,$$
then
$$\tau(A,B)
\leq\sum_i\lfloor N_i/6\rfloor
\leq\lfloor N/6\rfloor.$$
Consequently, any failure must have a connected component that itself violates the target.The two established boundary theorems then apply:All-square theorem: arbitrary owner paths and even cycles are covered when every auxiliary component is  $C_4$ .No-auxiliary- $C_4$  theorem: the owner-matching obstruction argument covers arbitrary auxiliary components when none is  $C_4$ .Both apply to the completed domain.Thus a remaining counterexample must contain both
$$C_4\quad\text{and}\quad C_{4k},\qquad k\geq2,$$
in its auxiliary decomposition, and must be connected under  $A\cup B$ .This is a necessary localization, not an existence result. It does not imply that an original counterexample remains connected or retains its original order after completion.3. The short-class quantitative refinementCorrect, with the stated two-copy scopeThis argument deserves separate treatment because it preserves information that the four-copy construction does not promise to preserve.Assume the original auxiliary components are only
$$P_2,\quad P_4,\quad C_4.$$
The two-copy completion turns:each  $P_2$  into a  $C_4$ ;each  $P_4$  into two  $C_4$ 's;each original  $C_4$  into two unchanged  $C_4$ 's.Thus the completed auxiliary graph is entirely a union of squares.The owner graph remains two disjoint copies of the original owner graph. In particular, for
$$R(B)=\sum_{\text{owner paths }K}|K|\bmod3,$$
including isolates, we have exactly
$$R(\widehat B)=2R(B).$$
The supplied refined square lemma on  $M$  indices gives an independent owner set  $S$ , dissociation in  $\widehat B$ , with
$$|S|\geq
\left\lceil\frac M3+\frac{R(\widehat B)}6\right\rceil.$$
Put  $\widehat U=\widehat V\setminus S$ . Because each auxiliary component is a square and  $S$  is independent in it,
$$\nu(\widehat A[\widehat U])
=\frac M2-|S|.$$
For  $M=2N$ , this yields
$$\nu(\widehat A[\widehat U])
\leq
\left\lfloor\frac{2N-2R(B)}6\right\rfloor.$$
Now apply the two-copy matching transfer:
$$\begin{aligned}
\min_j\nu(A[U_j])
&\leq
\left\lfloor
\frac{\lfloor(2N-2R(B))/6\rfloor}{2}
\right\rfloor\\
&=
\boxed{\left\lfloor\frac{N-R(B)}6\right\rfloor}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the requested quantitative strengthening.The four-copy version closes owner paths and changes the owner component structure. There is no corresponding assertion that its closure preserves the original  $R(B)$ . The quantitative conclusion belongs to the two-copy alternative only.The provenance distinction is appropriate: the original two-copy proposal is attributed to the independent Oracle research answer; the four-copy owner closure is a subsequent deduction.
